entries.text: Golden hour, weather included. Golden Hour remains the honest astronomical window, but today’s scene no longer promises visible gold through a solid cloud deck. Live cloud cover now moves both light tools from clear warmth through filtered light to an overcast grey-blue, softening the sun and moon as the sky closes. Golden Hour labels the current character of the light, shifts its color estimate and replaces flare-and-shadow advice with useful overcast guidance; Drone Weather reports cloud percentage beside the model conditions while keeping cloud cover separate from its safety verdict.

Weather after dark. Drone Weather’s original living field scene now follows Detroit’s local solar clock all the way through the day: an airy daytime wash warms toward sunset, cools through blue hour and settles into a deeper night palette across the sky, drone, tree, wind and wildlife. Its moon no longer substitutes for the sun or travels backward; it enters on its own left-to-right arc, may share the morning sky, and reflects the date’s waxing or waning crescent, quarter, gibbous, full or new phase.

Sun and moon, untangled. The Golden Hour sun now finishes its descent through the drawn horizon instead of fading and seeming to rise again. The moon follows its own left-to-right path, can share the daylight sky when the cycle calls for it, and wears the selected date’s new, crescent, quarter, gibbous or full phase with waxing or waning and illumination noted. Its arc remains a visual planning cue rather than a precise moonrise ephemeris.

Local film knowledge, connected. The LaB Assistant now knows that Scattered and Mistaken share the Detroit 48HFP Group B screening at 4:30 PM. It recognizes Mistaken as a joint ST Park Productions and Koffee Noir Productions short, can name Veda, Joe, Billy, Anton, Rylie, David, Jeremy, Brandon, Amber, Kate and Nikki as collaborators on it, and is careful not to invent individual roles that have not been recorded yet. Its notes also catch up with the current Golden Hour, Drone Weather, persistent checklist and Aspect Ratio tools instead of describing their earliest versions.

Golden Hour, framed tighter. The living sky is now a slim panoramic scene, keeping the time scrubber and all four light readings in the same view without losing the quote roller, moon, birds or wind. The selected date now settles into the open side of the hero, its introduction divides into two balanced thoughts, and the light windows rise closer to the planner. A fuller five-pine silhouette settles the right side of the frame while leaving the sun path open, and the motion remains calm when the timeline moves. The roller now travels through distinct, time-ordered filmmaking prompts from the last dark before dawn through morning gold, midday, evening gold, blue hour and late night. Colophon stories have also been pared back to the details worth keeping, with their key words carrying LaB’s ember italic accent.

Flight planning, kept close. The 18-point pre-flight checklist stays completely out of sight until requested beside the live conditions, then travels around the site until it is closed. Its higher-contrast, softly rounded field window remains movable, minimizable, browser-only and printable to PDF; it can now be resized on desktop and remembers those dimensions. Each six-item section earns its own restrained spark-and-glow celebration, and 18/18 finishes with Go fly. Drone Weather keeps its original animated ecosystem and follows the real Detroit solar clock without putting simulation controls over the scene; a faint, collapsed light preview remains for testing, and closing it returns immediately to live time. Gust-reading and night-flight notes tuck away until needed while the live thresholds remain planted in view. Golden Hour gets its own wide pixel scene with wind-driven pine tips, larger smoothly drifting birds and streaks, a true sun-to-moon handoff, and a higher, more legible quote roller with LaB’s orange italic ending.

Detroit 48HFP screenings added. The August 2 Group A and Group B premieres at the Redford Theater now carry both showtimes, one-click tickets, venue and map links; LaB’s Scattered, made as Sideways Lab, is marked for Group B at 4:30 PM. The August 16 Best Of screening and awards at the Civic Theater is listed separately, and both entries expire themselves after their screening date.

Golden Hour, rebuilt. The decorative fixed-time helper is now a real date-and-location-aware shoot planner: calculated blue and golden windows, sunrise, sunset, solar noon, elevation, direction, daylight, a scrub-able sun arc, a time-sensitive quote roller in the Story Generator style, and a copyable day plan. Drone Weather now reports actual Open-Meteo gusts, visibility and precipitation instead of estimates. Portfolio theme controls work again, lightbox keyboard focus behaves, runtime resource IDs stay unique, mobile overflow is gone, navigation and footers agree, and the public-but-tucked-away AI Usage link no longer enters the tab order. A real Chromium suite now patrols the kinds of failures static checks miss.

Maintenance pass. Story Generator tone tags no longer overwrite one another when an idea belongs to more than one mood. A 91-check CI suite now guards scripts, data, links, page structure, assistant coverage, social previews and published totals. The new tools respect reduced-motion settings, the weather scene stops drawing when it has nothing to animate, and lighter WebP hero images trim repeat page weight. The AI Usage dashboard stays public by URL but tucked behind its Easter eggs.

Housekeeping. The floating assistant was missing from Aspect Ratio, Golden Hour and Drone Weather since they shipped; all three have it now. The test that guards that had been failing on a hardcoded page count, so it never got as far as checking. Sitemap picked up the three tool pages, and the resource total was corrected to 127, having read 126 on five pages and 128 in the README since the last entry was added.

Themes renamed. Stone becomes Sepia, the warm-paper theme people actually mean by that word, and the dark weathered-wood theme that held the name becomes Timber. Saved preferences migrate automatically, so nobody flips between a light and dark page. 404 was quietly missing a theme button and now offers all five.

Drone Weather, part two. New pixel scene: wind you can actually read, gusts that arrive in bursts with real lulls instead of every two seconds, drizzle told apart from rain, and a sun that grows with the temperature. Deer, foxes, squirrels and rabbits wander through, and the drone breaks station to film them. The scene is no longer a box: its horizon is the page's own dividing line, tinted with the flight-safety state.

Flight safety, expanded. Why the gust number matters more than steady wind, what night flying actually requires, an 18-point pre-flight checklist that remembers itself in your browser, and links to the forecast services worth opening before a shoot.
AI Usage Dashboard launched. Secret Easter egg page with Konami code and hidden dot on Colophon.
Drone Weather rebuilt from scratch, with live rain detection via Open-Meteo, FPV drone flight physics, flocking birds, procedural tree sway, breathing sun glow, mouse-tracking pilot.
Golden Hour Helper : interactive shooting advice phrases, slot-machine spin animation, hero-sized sun arc.
Aspect Ratio Tool : local photo/video previewing, multi-file uploads, native aspect detection. Zero-upload privacy documented in Colophon.
Sepia theme added site-wide. Warm e-ink papyrus palette across all pages and theme bars. (Shipped as Stone; renamed 1 August.)
Colophon expanded with tool case studies. Stats counters updated. Two-column grid layout applied to details sections.
Story Generator expanded to 14 genre filters. Added printable field brief exporter and keyboard hotkeys.
Removed unfinished 'Still Available?' placeholder from portfolio and timeline.
LaB Assistant knowledgebase ingested, verifying film crew, gear, and production data. Video cards added to film queries. Mobile chat UI optimized.
About page reframed to emphasize team collaboration. Behind-the-scenes set knowledge added.
SkyBound restructured with Start Here path. Weather & Safety hero link added. Headlines restyled (sky blue + orange italic).
Drone Weather Guide created as standalone page. SkyBound restored. Golden Hour Helper dropdowns fixed.
Aspect Ratio Previewer tool page built. Live Drone Weather Flight Safety Meter added.
Static history section converted to Interactive Vertical Production Timeline with filtering and jump links.
Sun Arc & Golden Hour calculator tool launched for filmmakers and drone pilots.
Site design system unified to editorial direction. One stylesheet, one token set, one nav, one footer. Replaced 11 divergent style blocks.
